transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-20 16:00 UTC
Duration: 54 min
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Daniel Ortiz (Redwood SE), Rachel Lin (Cedar Head of ML), Tom Becker (CTO), Sara Gomez (Infra), Mike Yates (Product)

00:00 Alex (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining, we wanted to run through cost and performance stuff today, sounds like cedar's mainly trying to understand unit economics across hosted, dedicated, and private, is that right?
00:09 Rachel (Cedar): yeah exactly, hi Alex, thanks. our finance org set a target — roughly 30k a month cap for the model feature we plan to ship in Q3, we need to see how that maps to tokens and batch strategies.
00:22 Alex: great, totally reasonable. quick intros — daniel's our SE, he'll walk through batching/benchmark ideas. real quick, can you share current usage profile? token volume, seq lengths?
00:30 Tom (CTO): we have a mix. average request ~600 tokens (prompt+response), but tail goes to 2k on some analytics queries; estimate right now ~8-12M tokens/month for the feature if adoption goes well.
00:44 Daniel (SE): ok that helps. couple of things up front — hosted pricing is simplest: per-token with no infra management. dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools, commit discounts and predictable throughput, private is our VPC/on-prem option with a platform fee plus infra costs.
00:58 Rachel: can you give example numbers? like what does per-token look like across those?
01:05 Alex: sure, high level example (these are illustrative): hosted generation at about $0.0008 per token for large gen models. so 10M tokens -> ~8k. embeddings differ but not in scope for this feature. For dedicated with a 12-month commit we often see 30-50% effective discount once you factor reserved capacity and better amortized GPU costs — so equivalent unit could be ~ $0.00045-0.0006 per token depending on batch efficiency.
01:35 Mike (Product): wait those numbers feel low; are you including context caching or is that raw decode tokens?
01:41 Daniel: good question — that's raw token cost extrapolation. The real lever is batching + prefix/KV caching. With prefix caching and a lot of shared context we often reduce per-token work by 10-40% depending on hit rate. And batching (amortizing kernels) can cut GPU cycles; for small prompt lengths batching helps throughput without hurting tail latency if configured with latency SLOs.
02:05 Sara (Infra): what's the practical difference for us if we go dedicated? do we still pay per-token?
02:10 Alex: you still pay for inference usage, but dedicated is priced as a committed capacity model: you reserve a pool of GPUs (or equivalent) and we bill the capacity commitment plus a smaller per-token usage/overage. The benefit is predictability and a lower blended cost if you're at steady volume. Also dedicated gives you isolation and VPC peering options.
02:28 Tom: curious about burst — if we have spikes in traffic will we get throttled?
02:33 Daniel: Dedicated supports burst capacity and autoscaling, but burst is governed by the policy you pick. We can configure guaranteed throughput and a short-term burst buffer; fallback paths include routing to hosted variants or a smaller model.
02:45 Rachel: regulatory question — for private deployment we need KMS and audit logs; what's included?
02:50 Alex: Redwood Private includes a customer-managed control plane option, integrates with KMS/HSM and exports audit logs; there is an enterprise packaging and support fee on top of infra costs. We'll send the SOC2 and security docs.
03:05 Tom: back to numbers — so if we're targeting 30k/month and expect 10M tokens, our per-token budget is about $0.003, right? (laughs)
03:12 Mike: yeah, 30k/10M -> $0.003. but if adoption grows to 50M tokens we're under pressure.
03:18 Alex: right, that's the math. If your internal target is $0.003 per token, hosted is fine for lower volume but you'd quickly get better economics with Reserved Dedicated or a private deployment. Example scenarios:
03:31 Alex: Scenario A — Hosted: $0.0008/token -> 10M tokens = $8k; 50M = $40k.
03:40 Alex: Scenario B — Dedicated (12m commit, 4x A100 equiv pool): blended $0.0005/token -> 10M = $5k; 50M = $25k. These are simplified but show how commit discounts scale.
03:54 Rachel: those Dedicated numbers seem favorable, but what's the up-front or platform fee?
03:58 Alex: Dedicated has a monthly capacity charge based on reserved GPUs. For small pilots we can do a light reserved pool plus burst into hosted. For private, there's a platform license (one-time or annual) and infra OPEX as usual. We'll put concrete dollar examples in the pricing sheet.
04:15 Tom: ok. what about batching — if we crank batch sizes to maximize throughput, what's the risk to latency? our product SLO is 95th < 500ms for interactive sessions.
04:24 Daniel: interactive sessions with 500ms 95th are tight; large batches increase efficiency but hurt p99/95 if you wait to fill the batch. Our runtime supports dynamic batching and latency-aware batching so you can prioritize latency SLOs. Typical approach: small batch windows for interactive, bigger batches for background jobs. Also kernel selection and quantization help.
04:42 Rachel: can you quantify savings from caching?
04:44 Daniel: rough rule — if you have repeat prompts or long shared prefixes, prefix/KV caching can reduce compute by 20-60% depending on hit rate. Example: an analytics query that reuses a 300-token prefix across users — that prefix isn't re-computed if cached.
04:58 Mike: what's required from our side to get good cache hit rates?
05:02 Daniel: stable prompt templates, consistent session ids, and controlling tokenization variability help. We can instrument a pilot to show expected hit rate given your traces.
05:11 Tom: ok, pilot idea — we could provide a week of traces and run a 2-week benchmark on a dedicated pool you size. what's the minimum pool?
05:19 Alex: depends on concurrency and latency. for 95th 500ms and your tail lengths we might start with 2-4 A100 equiv for the pilot. we'll size in the deep dive.
05:28 Rachel: procurement question — if we sign a 12-month commit and then need to scale down, are there flex terms?
05:33 Alex: yes, we offer a few flexible commit terms — you can choose monthly step-down windows and negotiated credits. We'll include the standard commitment language in the sheet.
05:43 Daniel: also worth noting model variant fallback — if a larger model is expensive, we can route to a slightly smaller quantized variant automatically during peak to maintain availability. That helps cost budgets.
05:56 Mike: any special discount for startups or non-profits? not relevant for cedar but curious —
06:00 Alex: we have enterprise pricing and occasional promotional credits for pilots; primary lever is committed capacity discount.
06:07 Tom: security follow-up — does dedicated or hosted keep logs? we need retention for audits and ability to redact PII.
06:13 Alex: we provide configurable retention and can integrate with your SIEM. For Private deployments you control logs; for Hosted/Dedicated we provide audit export and redaction tools. We'll attach the security pack.
06:25 Rachel: ok, this is helpful. one more nit: how do you measure "effective per-token" when you have caching and batching?
06:33 Daniel: we report token accounting and effective GPU seconds per token in the benchmark. The pricing sheet will include both nominal per-token price and an example of effective unit cost after caching/batching for your trace profile.
06:45 Mike: what's a plausible blended unit cost if we optimize caching well?
06:49 Daniel: for a workload with 30% cache hit rate and moderate batching, you could see 30-40% lower effective cost versus raw per-token. So if raw is $0.0008, effective could be ~$0.0005.
07:01 Tom: that helps. what's the timeline for the pilot? we're targeting shipping a limited beta in late June.
07:06 Alex: we can propose a 2-week pilot in May to validate perf and cost, then a 12-week ramp before beta.
07:12 Rachel: decision makers include me and Tom, also finance will review the model. we'll need a clear runbook for the pilot.
07:20 Alex: noted. action items and we'll follow up with a formal pricing deck + benchmark plan.
07:25 (crosstalk)
07:28 Alex: quick recap: 1) we'll send Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private pricing scenarios, 2) Daniel will send batching/caching whitepaper and benchmark plan, 3) Cedar shares traces and SLOs, 4) schedule technical deep dive week of Apr 27.
07:43 Tom: sounds good, thanks.
07:45 Rachel: thanks everyone.
07:47 Alex: thanks, we'll follow up.

End of transcript.
